items.name: "Forania" indet.
items.basis: Forania is a zosterophyll with branched, spinose axes and lateral bivalved sporangia.
items.source: [Jensen & Gensel (2013), Forania plegiospinosa: A Zosterophyll from the Early Devonian](https://www.journals.uchicago.edu/doi/pdfplus/10.1086/669914), abstract.

items.name: <"Kaulangiophyton">
items.basis: Kaulangiophyton comprises branched shoots bearing sporangia and is assigned to the zosterophyll lineage.
items.source: [USGS, Index of Generic Names of Fossil Plants, 1966–1973, Kaulangiophyton entry](https://pubs.usgs.gov/bul/1396/report.pdf), indexed passage.

items.name: <"Leclercqia">
items.basis: Leclercqia is a microphyllous lycopsid; ligules are documented in its type species.
items.source: [Grierson & Bonamo (1979), Leclercqia complexa: Earliest Ligulate Lycopod](https://bsapubs.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1002/j.1537-2197.1979.tb06248.x).

items.name: <"Leclerqia">
items.basis: Interpreted as a misspelling of Leclercqia, the ligulate lycopsid, rather than a distinct genus.
items.source: [Grierson & Bonamo (1979), Leclercqia complexa: Earliest Ligulate Lycopod](https://bsapubs.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1002/j.1537-2197.1979.tb06248.x).

items.name: <Articulale>
items.basis: The extract records a sterile axis; the informal label does not establish articulated sphenopsid morphology or vascular anatomy.
items.source: none checked

items.name: <Lycopsids>
items.basis: The identification explicitly denotes lycopsids; these flags classify that named group, conditional on the sterile-axis identification.
items.source: [Claisse et al. (2025), Re-evaluating the phylogenetic relationships of zosterophylls](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13274996/).

items.name: <Morphotype I>
items.basis: An anonymous sterile-axis morphotype supplies no diagnostic reproductive or anatomical evidence for a vascular lineage.
items.source: none checked

items.name: <Morphotype II>
items.basis: The sterile-axis record and anonymous morphotype label do not establish sporangia, tracheids or a particular land-plant lineage.
items.source: none checked

items.name: <Morphotype III>
items.basis: Published material assigned to Tanner's morphotype III consists of axes radiating from a common attachment; diagnostic fertility and vascular anatomy remain unestablished.
items.source: [Caruso & Tomescu (2012), Microconchid encrusters colonizing land plants](https://mihaibotany.online/pdf/Caruso%202012%20Lethaia.pdf), text and figure 1F–G.

items.name: <Trimerophyte>
items.basis: Trimerophytes are basal euphyllophytes. This classifies the informal group identification without independently validating the occurrence.
items.source: [Cantino et al. (2007), Towards a phylogenetic nomenclature of Tracheophyta](https://donoghuelab.yale.edu/sites/default/files/165_cantino_taxon07.pdf), discussion of Pan-Euphyllophyta.

items.name: <zosterophylloid>
items.basis: The label denotes a zosterophyll; the Canadian zosterophylloid-axis material was subsequently associated with Bathurstia denticulata.
items.source: [Kotyk (1998), Late Silurian and Early Devonian fossil plants of Bathurst Island](https://harvest.usask.ca/bitstreams/518d9179-7afe-4dd9-88b1-1833d37449e8/download), indexed primary-text passages.

items.name: ? Euomphalopteris sp.
items.basis: Euomphalopteris is a marine gastropod name appearing in the original Alaskan faunal list. This is non-plant contamination of the extract, rather than an anomalously aged land plant.
items.source: [USGS Professional Paper 87, Geology of the Hanagita–Bremner Region and southeastern Alaska contributions](https://pubs.usgs.gov/pp/0087/report.pdf), Kasaan Peninsula faunal list, p. 71, indexed passage.

items.name: ? Pachytheca sp.
items.basis: Pachytheca comprises small spheres with differentiated filamentous tissues and conjectural, commonly algal affinities; it is not an accepted embryophyte.
items.source: [Gerrienne, Les Pachytheca de La Gileppe et de Nonceveux](https://popups.ulg.ac.be/0037-9395/index.php?id=1298&lang=en), published abstract.

items.name: ? Protaxites loganii
items.basis: Interpreted as a misspelling of Prototaxites loganii, a tubular, non-vascular problematic organism rather than a branched embryophyte sporophyte.
items.source: [Retallack & Landing (2014), Affinities and architecture of Devonian trunks of Prototaxites loganii](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/24990121/), abstract.

items.name: ? Protoarticulata indet.
items.basis: Høeg's material consists of axes with irregular verticils and possible leaf bases, explicitly retained incertae sedis despite comparison with Hyenia.
items.source: [Høeg (1942), The Downtonian and Devonian flora of Spitsbergen](https://brage.npolar.no/npolar-xmlui/bitstream/handle/11250/173926/Skrifter083.pdf?isAllowed=y&sequence=1), p. 88, indexed passage.

items.name: ? Psilophyte indet.
items.basis: The historical specimen is a slender axis with two isotomous bifurcations, subsequently compared with Hostinella; diagnostic fertility is lacking.
items.source: [Prestianni et al. (2012), Review of Palaeobotany and Palynology 179:44–55](https://orbi.uliege.be/bitstream/2268/137700/1/Prestiannietal2012.pdf), section 5.5.2.

items.name: Aarabia brevicaulis n. gen. n. sp.
items.basis: Pseudomonopodial shoots bear differentiated lateral branching systems and elongate terminal sporangia; the published analysis associates Aarabia with basal euphyllophytes.
items.source: [Meyer-Berthaud & Gerrienne (2001), Aarabia, a new Early Devonian vascular plant from Africa](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S003466670100063X), abstract and conclusion.

items.name: Aberlemnia sp.
items.basis: Aberlemnia has dichotomous axes with terminal, bivalved sporangia and is interpreted as a basal member of Lycophytina.
items.source: [Libertín, Kvaček & Bek (2024), The genus Aberlemnia and its Silurian–Devonian fossil record](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S0034666723001860), abstract and highlights.

items.name: Actinophyllum
items.basis: The historical fossil was compared with an alga, but the consulted geological account retains uncertain affinity; secure embryophyte characters are not established.
items.source: [Cleal & Thomas, Palaeozoic Palaeobotany of Great Britain, Silurian chapter](https://data.jncc.gov.uk/data/a2ed7572-87e2-40b9-93cf-2f3af82d8797/gcr-v9-palaeozoic-palaeobotany-of-great-britain-c3.pdf), Actinophyllum discussion.

items.name: Actinopodium nathorstii
items.basis: Permineralised axes have a stellate vascular system and secondary xylem; Actinopodium is included among archaeopteridalean progymnosperms.
items.source: [Cornet et al. (2012), A Middle Devonian Callixylon from Ronquières, Belgium](https://orbi.uliege.be/bitstream/2268/129376/1/Cornet%20et%20al.,%202012..pdf), introduction.

items.name: Anaeurophyton germanicum
items.basis: Interpreted as a spelling error for Aneurophyton germanicum, an aneurophytalean progymnosperm with complex branching systems and woody axes.
items.source: [Krings (2024), Branch system of a progymnosperm, Bavarian State Collection](https://bspg.snsb.de/oktober-2024-xxx/?lang=en).

items.name: Anapaulia moodyi
items.basis: Whorled branching systems and dichotomising appendages support the published interpretation as a probable iridopteridalean.
items.source: [Berry & Edwards (1996), Anapaulia moodyi: a probable iridopteridalean compression fossil](https://orca.cardiff.ac.uk/id/eprint/10072/), abstract.

items.name: Aneurophytales
items.basis: Aneurophytales are woody, spore-producing progymnosperms on the euphyllophyte lineage.
items.source: [Krings (2024), Branch system of a progymnosperm](https://bspg.snsb.de/oktober-2024-xxx/?lang=en).

items.name: Aneurophyton germanicum
items.basis: Aneurophyton germanicum is an aneurophytalean progymnosperm with spirally arranged, repeatedly divided branching systems.
items.source: [Krings (2024), Branch system of a progymnosperm](https://bspg.snsb.de/oktober-2024-xxx/?lang=en).

items.name: Aneurophyton hallii
items.basis: Material historically assigned this name includes the woody aneurophytalean subsequently revised as Triloboxylon arnoldii; species-level synonymy requires care.
items.source: [Stein & Beck (1983), Triloboxylon arnoldii from the Middle Devonian of Western New York](https://deepblue.lib.umich.edu/bitstream/2027.42/48520/2/ID372.pdf), indexed abstract and synonymy.

items.name: Angarolaminariopsis zinovae
items.basis: The consulted account records its provisional assignment to Laminariales; this supports an algal interpretation without establishing that it was a true kelp.
items.source: [Zerov (1972), Essay on the phylogeny of non-vascular plants](https://ru.djvu.online/file/HkY3t7gfb3lE0), indexed digitised text discussing Ananiev's material.

items.name: Anisophyton cf. gothanii
items.basis: Anisophyton is placed within the sawdoniaceous zosterophylls; the species comparison remains provisional.
items.source: [Claisse et al. (2025)](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13274996/), phylogeny and illustrated Anisophyton material.

items.name: Aphyllopteris
items.basis: Aphyllopteris is a form-genus for incomplete leafless branching axes; its architecture alone does not establish a particular vascular lineage.
items.source: [Høeg (1952), Psilophytites, a new form genus of Devonian plants](https://journals.sagepub.com/doi/pdf/10.54991/jop.1952.409), indexed discussion of Aphyllopteris.

items.name: Archaeosigillaria
items.basis: Archaeosigillaria is a lycopsid genus, although revision has reassigned some historically included species.
items.source: [Berry & Edwards (1997), A new species of Gilboaphyton, with a revision of Archaeosigillaria](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0034666796000152).

items.name: Asterocalamites
items.basis: This archaeocalamitalean sphenopsid has a documented range beginning in the Late Devonian; the Pragian identification requires correction.
items.source: [Newfoundland Geological Survey, Current Research (1999), Boyce contribution](https://www.gov.nl.ca/em/files/mines-geoscience-publications-currentresearch-1999-boyce.pdf), indexed Asterocalamites/Archaeocalamites discussion.

items.name: Asteroxylon
items.basis: Anatomically demonstrated drepanophycalean lycopsid with leafy shoots and differentiated rooting systems.
items.source: [Hetherington et al. (2021), Asteroxylon reconstruction and rooting-system study](https://elifesciences.org/articles/69447).

items.name: Baragwanathia
items.basis: Microphyllous shoots and vascular anatomy establish lycopsid affinity; disputed earliest occurrence ages do not alter this placement.
items.source: [Selden & Edwards, Colonisation of the land](https://www.paulselden.net/uploads/7/5/3/2/7532217/colonisation.pdf), Baragwanathia discussion.

items.name: Baragwanathia longifolia
items.basis: Its microphyllous morphology and anatomy support lycopsid placement; the debated dating of particular Australian records is a separate issue.
items.source: [Selden & Edwards, Colonisation of the land](https://www.paulselden.net/uploads/7/5/3/2/7532217/colonisation.pdf).

items.name: Baragwanthia longifolia
items.basis: The Australian context identifies this as a spelling variant of Baragwanathia longifolia, a microphyllous lycopsid.
items.source: [Selden & Edwards, Colonisation of the land](https://www.paulselden.net/uploads/7/5/3/2/7532217/colonisation.pdf).

items.name: Barinophyton
items.basis: Recent phylogenetic analyses place barinophytes within Lycophytina, among the zosterophyll grade.
items.source: [Claisse et al. (2025)](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13274996/).

items.name: Barsassia ornata
items.basis: Modern revision identifies a herbaceous lycopsid with imbricate leaves and vascular anatomy, superseding the legacy psilophyte grouping.
items.source: [Liu et al. (2021), Barsassia morphology and nomenclatural revision](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8703484/).

items.name: Bathurstia cf. denticulata
items.basis: Bathurstia is a zosterophyll within Lycophytina; the species identification is explicitly tentative.
items.source: [Claisse et al. (2025)](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13274996/).

items.name: Bathurstia denticulata n. gen. n. sp.
items.basis: Bathurstia is recovered within Lycophytina, close to the barinophytes.
items.source: [Claisse et al. (2025)](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13274996/).

items.name: Bathurstia sp.
items.basis: The genus denotes a zosterophyll; its identification from this axis remains conditional.
items.source: [Claisse et al. (2025)](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13274996/).

items.name: Bergeria
items.basis: The identified B. mimerensis material consists of lepidophytic stems with leaf cushions; its precise relationship to other Devonian lycopsids remains unresolved.
items.source: [Høeg (1942), The Downtonian and Devonian flora of Spitsbergen](https://brage.npolar.no/npolar-xmlui/bitstream/handle/11250/173926/Skrifter083.pdf?isAllowed=y&sequence=1), original-description excerpts.

items.name: Bitelaria dubjanskii
items.basis: Canadian material was reinterpreted as a vascular land plant rather than an alga, but its position relative to the lycophyte–euphyllophyte split remains unresolved.
items.source: [Johnson & Gensel (1992), Bitelaria study](https://eurekamag.com/research/008/071/008071253.php); [published abstract reproduced](https://documentsdelivered.com/source/018/452/018452481.php).

items.name: Blasaria
items.basis: Blasaria was founded on lycopod leaf-base impressions; the named genus supports lycophyte affinity, with incomplete evidence for every included species.
items.source: [USGS generic index, Blasaria entry](https://pubs.usgs.gov/bul/1013/report.pdf); [Liu et al. (2021), comparison with Barsassia](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8703484/).

items.name: Bowerophylloides mendozaensis
items.basis: The original account describes sterile leafy axes that cannot be unequivocally assigned to established taxa; reproductive and diagnostic vascular characters are lacking.
items.source: [Edwards et al. (2001), Bowerophylloides original account](https://orca.cardiff.ac.uk/id/eprint/10065/), abstract.

items.name: Caia langii n. gen. n. sp.
items.basis: Dichotomous naked axes terminate in elongate sporangia containing trilete spores; comparison with Horneophyton supports rhyniophytoid organisation.
items.source: [Fanning et al. (1990), Caia original description](https://orca.cardiff.ac.uk/id/eprint/10177/), abstract.

items.name: Calamophyton
items.basis: Calamophyton is a pseudosporochnalean cladoxylopsid reconstructed from connected trunks, branching crowns and roots.
items.source: [Giesen & Berry (2013), Calamophyton whole-plant reconstruction](https://orca.cardiff.ac.uk/id/eprint/47293/), abstract.

items.name: Calamophyton primaevum
items.basis: This genuine Middle Devonian species is a cladoxylopsid with organically connected trunk, crown and rooting structures.
items.source: [Giesen & Berry (2013), Calamophyton whole-plant reconstruction](https://orca.cardiff.ac.uk/id/eprint/47293/).

items.name: Callixylon
items.basis: Callixylon denotes archaeopteridalean progymnosperm wood, characterised by grouped tracheid pitting. PBDB's cordaitalean placement is inappropriate.
items.source: [Cornet et al. (2012), A Middle Devonian Callixylon from Ronquières, Belgium](https://orbi.uliege.be/bitstream/2268/129376/1/Cornet%20et%20al.,%202012..pdf).

items.name: Catenalis digitata
items.basis: The original account describes branched axes with putative sporangia but cannot establish typical tracheids and entertains both algal and vascular-plant interpretations.
items.source: [Hao & Beck (1991), Catenalis digitata](https://www.researchgate.net/publication/237164533_Catenalis_digitata_gen_et_spnov_a_plant_from_the_Lower_Devonian_Siegenian_of_Yunnan_China), reproduced abstract.

items.name: Caulopteris
items.basis: The identified Devonian species were described as fern-like stems with petiole or leaf-scar characters; broad euphyllophyte affinity is more defensible than a specific marattialean assignment.
items.source: [Dawson (1888), The Geological History of Plants](https://readingroo.ms/5/1/0/2/51021/51021-h/51021-h.htm), descriptions of Devonian Caulopteris.

items.name: Cephalopteris
items.basis: The actual identification is C. praecox, subsequently Protocephalopteris praecox, a Devonian fern-like plant; it should not inherit the old genus's seed-fern assignment.
items.source: [Xue & Basinger (2016), Melvillipteris quadriseriata](https://www.researchgate.net/publication/283145584_Melvillipteris_quadriseriata_gen_et_sp_nov_a_new_plant_from_the_Upper_Devonian_Famennian_of_Arctic_Canada), published comparison.

items.name: Chaleuria cirrosa
items.basis: Monopodial axes bear dichotomous ultimate branches and paired terminal sporangia; the original authors suggested primitive progymnosperm affinities.
items.source: [Andrews, Gensel & Forbes (1974), An apparently heterosporous plant from the Middle Devonian of New Brunswick](https://palass.org/sites/default/files/media/publications/palaeontology/volume_17/vol17_part2_pp387-408.pdf).

items.name: Chauvinia scharyana
items.basis: This historical fossil name denotes Protolepidodendron scharianum material with lepidodendroid shoots and narrow, sometimes divided leaves, rather than the living algal homonym.
items.source: [USGS generic index, Chauvinia entry](https://pubs.usgs.gov/bul/1300/report.pdf); [Jahn (1903), description and synonymy](https://opac.geologie.ac.at/ais312/dokumente/Verh_kk_geol_RA_1903_komplett.pdf), indexed passages.

items.name: Ciguelia juvenile n. gen. n. sp.
items.basis: The original abstract groups Ciguelia among sterile, simply dichotomising axes; diagnostic fertility and vascular anatomy are not established in the consulted material.
items.source: [Mussa et al. (1996), original abstract reproduced on this literature page](https://www.researchgate.net/publication/326217684_EARLY_DEVONIAN_TAPHOFLORA_RECORD_IN_PONTA_GROSSA_ARCH_PARANA_BASIN_SOUTHERN_BRAZIL_AND_ITS_PALAEOGEOGRAPHIC_IMPLICATIONS_REGISTRO_DA_TAFOFLORA_DEVONIANA_NO_ARCO_DE_PONTA_GROSSA_BACIA_DO_PARANA_SUL_DO_).

items.name: Cladophlebis
items.basis: Cladophlebis is a younger fern-foliage morphogenus, particularly characteristic of Mesozoic floras; the enormous collection-age interval does not establish an early Palaeozoic occurrence.
items.source: [Jud et al. (2013), discussion of Cladophlebis foliage](https://bsapubs.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/full/10.3732/ajb.1200637).

items.name: Cladoxylon
items.basis: The identified C. scoparium is a genuine Devonian cladoxylopsid, associated in modern reconstruction with Calamophyton primaevum.
items.source: [Giesen & Berry (2013), Calamophyton reconstruction and synonymy](https://orca.cardiff.ac.uk/id/eprint/47293/).

items.name: Cladoxylopsida
items.basis: Cladoxylopsids are euphyllophytes, despite continuing uncertainty over their relationships within that lineage.
items.source: [Durieux et al. (2026), Systematics and evolution of cladoxylopsids](https://www.cambridge.org/core/journals/journal-of-paleontology/article/systematics-and-evolution-of-cladoxylopsids-a-consequential-yet-underappreciated-tracheophyte-group-with-a-deep-fossil-history/BA2D34F54ABDA687AFA0672771F708E5).

items.name: Coactilum
items.basis: A calcimicrobe traditionally treated as a schizophyte alga and referred to Rothpletzella; precise microbial affinity is uncertain, but embryophyte affinity is unsupported.
items.source: [Liu et al. (2016), Tarim calcimicrobe systematic account](https://robertriding.com/pdf/liu-etal-2016-tarim.pdf).

items.name: Codonophycus austinii
items.basis: The taxon is an alga described from the Mississippian Madison Formation; the broad PBDB interval supplies no evidence of a Devonian occurrence.
items.source: [USGS generic index, Codonophycus entry, p. 56](https://digital.library.unt.edu/ark%3A/67531/metadc1114957/m1/62/), indexed entry.

items.name: Colpodexylon
items.basis: A protolepidodendralean lycopsid with characteristically divided microphylls.
items.source: [Edwards & Benedetto (1985), Devonian lycophyte systematic account](https://palass.org/sites/default/files/media/publications/palaeontology/volume_28/vol28_part3_pp599-618.pdf).

items.name: Colpodexylon deatsii
items.basis: The lycopsid type species has lobed xylem and trifurcate leaves. Its Frasnian type record warrants checking this particular Middle Devonian identification.
items.source: [Edwards & Benedetto (1985)](https://palass.org/sites/default/files/media/publications/palaeontology/volume_28/vol28_part3_pp599-618.pdf), Colpodexylon comparison.

items.name: Compsocradus laevigatus
items.basis: An anatomically documented iridopteridalean with a six-ribbed mesarch vascular system and complex lateral branching.
items.source: [Berry & Stein (2000), Compsocradus laevigatus](https://www.journals.uchicago.edu/doi/abs/10.1086/314295), abstract.

items.name: Conchulophyton quadrosii n. gen. n. sp.
items.basis: Bibliographic metadata confirms the name, but no diagnostic description was recovered; its Furnas provenance alone cannot establish biological affinity.
items.source: [Mussa et al. (2002), New taxa from the Furnas Formation: institutional catalogue](https://www.infraestruturameioambiente.sp.gov.br/institutodebotanica/2002/01/new-taxa-from-the-furnas-formation-parana-basin-brasil-an-approach-and-revalidation-of-names/), metadata only.

items.name: Cooksonia
items.basis: Branched sporophytes bear terminal sporangia; heterogeneous historical usage and unresolved phylogenetic placement prevent a secure crown-tracheophyte assignment.
items.source: Gonez & Gerrienne (2010), A new definition and a lectotypification of the genus Cooksonia Lang 1937, International Journal of Plant Sciences 171:199–215; full local PDF consulted.

items.name: Cooksonia hemisphaerica
items.basis: Branched axes terminate in hemispherical sporangia; poor preservation leaves its precise systematic position unresolved.
items.source: Gonez & Gerrienne (2010), A new definition and a lectotypification of the genus Cooksonia Lang 1937, International Journal of Plant Sciences 171:199–215; full local PDF consulted.

items.name: Cooksonia pertoni
items.basis: Tracheids establish vascular status, but published phylogenetic analyses do not securely settle placement relative to the crown-tracheophyte node.
items.source: Gonez & Gerrienne (2010), A new definition and a lectotypification of the genus Cooksonia Lang 1937, International Journal of Plant Sciences 171:199–215; full local PDF consulted.

items.name: Crenaticaulis
items.basis: A sawdoniaceous zosterophyll within Lycophytina.
items.source: [Claisse et al. (2025)](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13274996/).

items.name: Cryptoxylon forfarense
items.basis: Kidston and Lang transferred this fossil to Nematophyton; its pseudoparenchymatous organisation does not represent vascular wood.
items.source: [Kidston & Lang (1924), Notes on fossil plants from the Old Red Sandstone of Scotland: Nematophyton forfarense](https://www.cambridge.org/core/journals/earth-and-environmental-science-transactions-of-royal-society-of-edinburgh/article/abs/xxixnotes-on-fossil-plants-from-the-old-red-sandstone-of-scotland-ii-nematophyton-forfarense-kidston-sp-iii-on-two-species-of-pachytheca-p-media-and-p-fasciculata-based-on-the-characters-of-the-algal-filaments/70862AE7D7A9C1D5A6F6B08DB13A7D7F), extract.

items.name: Dadoxylon
items.basis: The identified D. cf. halli denotes secondary wood consistent with a lignophyte; its precise whole-plant association remains unproved.
items.source: [Knowlton, Revision of Araucarioxylon](https://repository.si.edu/bitstreams/66b52b0c-1ca2-460b-a6b4-f8c86a6da839/download), discussion of Dadoxylon halli.

items.name: Dalejophyton nemejci
items.basis: A later assessment interprets the supposed sporangia as probably unflattened coiled sterile tips; anatomy and epidermal characters remain unknown.
items.source: [Broushkin & Gordenko, Istchenkophyton filiciforme](https://www.researchgate.net/publication/225638287_Istchenkophyton_filiciforme_gen_et_sp_nov_a_New_Small_Vascular_Plant_with_Thick_Cuticle_from_the_Devonian_of_Voronezh_Region_European_Russia), published comparison excerpt.

items.name: Dawsonites
items.basis: A form-genus for isolated fertile branching systems resembling Psilophyton and other basal euphyllophytes, rather than a securely reconstructed natural genus.
items.source: [Revisiting the Rebreuve plant assemblage from the Lower Devonian of Artois](https://orbi.uliege.be/bitstream/2268/302489/1/Revisiting%20the%20Rebreuve%20plant%20assemblage%20from%20the%20Lower%20Devonian%20of%20Artois%20northern%20France.pdf), Dawsonites discussion.

items.name: Dawsonites arcuatus
items.basis: Clusters of pendulous fusiform sporangia are interpreted as trimerophyte fertile organs; some better-characterised material has been reassigned to Psilophyton.
items.source: [Revisiting the Rebreuve plant assemblage from the Lower Devonian of Artois](https://orbi.uliege.be/bitstream/2268/302489/1/Revisiting%20the%20Rebreuve%20plant%20assemblage%20from%20the%20Lower%20Devonian%20of%20Artois%20northern%20France.pdf).

items.name: Distichophytum
items.basis: A zosterophyll recovered within Lycophytina in recent analyses.
items.source: [Claisse et al. (2025)](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13274996/).

items.name: Drepanophycus
items.basis: A microphyllous lycopsid, despite its legacy PBDB psilophyte grouping.
items.source: [Claisse et al. (2025)](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13274996/).

items.name: Drepanophycus gaspianus
items.basis: A microphyllous lycophyte; predominantly vegetative material and poorly known fertility complicate discrimination from related genera.
items.source: [Li & Edwards (1997), published abstract](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/21708551/); [Kotyk (1998), Bathurst Island fossil plants](https://harvest.usask.ca/bitstream/handle/10388/12414/Kotyk_Michelle_Elizabeth_Ann_1998_sec.pdf?isAllowed=y&sequence=1), pp. 63–64.

items.name: Drepanophycus spinaeformis
items.basis: An anatomically documented lycophyte with protostelic xylem and annular or helical tracheids.
items.source: [The effect of pyrite on the tracheid structure of Drepanophycus spinaeformis (1981)](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/0034666781900063), abstract.

items.name: Dutoitea
items.basis: The actual identification, D. maraisia, concerns Famennian material; modern revision rejects its rhyniophytoid attribution and compares its fertile appendages with Flabellopteris.
items.source: [Gess & Prestianni, Flabellopteris lococannensis](https://orbi.uliege.be/bitstream/2268/302493/1/1-s2.0-S0034666721002098-main.pdf), section 7.

items.name: Dutoitia
items.basis: The identified D. alfreda was described as a branched plant with terminal sporangia, but its relationship to the rhyniophytoid type species and vascular lineages remains uncertain.
items.source: [Plumstead (1967), original description of Dutoitia alfreda](https://wiredspace.wits.ac.za/bitstreams/9fdfc1a6-f6a5-4295-b5a8-da67d61127d0/download), indexed text and [plate I](https://wiredspace.wits.ac.za/bitstreams/938bc525-ad4f-4760-a2b2-ed82d61657d5/download).

items.name: Dutoitia pulchra
items.basis: The type species has rhyniophytoid organisation; modern reassessment places its locality in the probably Lochkovian Baviaanskloof Formation, contrary to the extract's broad younger interval.
items.source: [Gess & Prestianni (2021), An early Devonian flora from the Baviaanskloof Formation](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8178408/).

items.name: Enigmophyton
items.basis: A large fan-leaved vascular-plant morphotype of unresolved affinity; associated reproductive organs should not be transferred to it without organic connection.
items.source: [Svalbard plants and sediments study (2021)](https://orca.cardiff.ac.uk/id/eprint/140269/1/JGS%20Accepted%20Svalbard%20Plants%20and%20Sediments%202021.pdf), table 2; [Bateman & DiMichele (1994)](https://repository.si.edu/bitstream/handle/10088/7107/paleo_1994_BatemanDiMichele_Heterospory_BiolRev_small.pdf), p. 381.

items.name: Enigmophyton superbum
items.basis: The foliage plant's precise affinity is unresolved; supposedly associated heterosporous fructifications lack organic connection and may belong to Barinophyton.
items.source: [Bateman & DiMichele (1994), Heterospory: the most iterative key innovation in the evolutionary history of the plant kingdom](https://repository.si.edu/bitstream/handle/10088/7107/paleo_1994_BatemanDiMichele_Heterospory_BiolRev_small.pdf), p. 381.

items.name: Eocooksonia
items.basis: Revised material has branching systems terminating in sporangia with triangular emergences; this supports rhyniophytoid organisation rather than unquestioned inheritance of PBDB's zosterophyll placement.
items.source: [Xue et al. (2015), New observations of the early land plant Eocooksonia from the Pridoli of Xinjiang](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jseaes.2015.02.003), abstract consulted through the Peking University institutional index.
